intro: El Salvador is the smallest and most densely populated country in Central America, a land of volcanoes and surf.

chapters.title: Joya de Cerén
text: About 1,400 years ago a volcanic eruption buried the Maya farming village of Joya de Cerén in ash, preserving homes, gardens and even food. It is called the 'Pompeii of the Americas'.

highlight.title: Frozen in time
highlight.text: Joya de Cerén shows everyday life of ordinary Maya farmers.

chapters.title: Pipil and Spanish rule
text: The Pipil people called their land Cuscatlán. Spain conquered it in the 1520s. El Salvador became independent in 1821.

chapters.title: War and change
text: A civil war from 1980 to 1992 killed about 75,000 people; Archbishop Óscar Romero was assassinated in 1980 and later made a saint. After the war, gangs grew. Since 2022 President Nayib Bukele's state of emergency has jailed tens of thousands of suspected gang members, cutting murders sharply but drawing human rights criticism.

keyTerms.meaning: Special powers given to the government.
